newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi shares ease as foreign buying slows down.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi shares ease as foreign buying slows down.

text.p: A notable absence of foreign demand for blue-chip stocks at the Nairobi Stock Exchange pulled down prices marginally on Friday, brokers and bourse officials said.
The NSE 20-share index shed 15.6 points to close at 3503.68. Turnover was posted at 15.5 million shillings traded on 356,719 shares compared to 41 million shillings on 478,299 shares.
Kenya Commercial Bank, largely supported by foreigners and the main mover in the market in the past few weeks, was down nine shillings to close at 101.
"The order we had for the share got finished," said a broker from the trading house with the leading number of foreign orders. "Local demand cannot support the share at that high price."
Barclays Bank eased to 110 from 112 while Standard Chartered Bank closed at 47.75 from 48.
Foreigners bought East African Portland Cement at a 42 from 40 and National Industrial Credit at 63.50 from 63.
Rea Vipingo Plantations fell to 10.05 from 10.10.
Kenya Airways edged to 8.25 from 8.20 while Uchumi Supermarket closed at 38.25 from 38.50.
Kenya Power & Lighting gained a shilling to close at 173 from 172 while Kenya Breweries closed at 57 from 57.50.
The Central Bank of Kenya floating-rate treasury bond traded 47.25 million shillings between 100.7685 and 100.77 percent from Thursday's close of 100.6550 percent.
